title: First position: SI, the rest in USDC
text:
Plan started with 1.98 SOL ($200). The memecoin market is weak today: of twelve large memecoins we checked (POPCAT, BONK peers, PNUT, MOODENG, TROLL, PUMP and others), ten trade below their 20-day average. Buying into that is how balanced plans lose money, so this plan starts small.

One position: SI ($14.3M market cap, 52K holders, top 10 hold 11%, $506K liquidity), the only mid-cap that passed every filter today: real trading volume, spread-out holders and a clean anti-rug check. About 30% of the plan.

The rest goes to USDC so it does not lose value if SOL keeps falling (SOL is 4% below its 20-day average). We will add positions as soon as candidates pass the filters; the next review is tonight.

Devil's advocate: SI's creator has launched about 7,500 tokens, typical of a token factory, and SI is up 45% in three days. We accept it because the holders are spread out and the stop is 20%.

title: Trend is down: holding USDC
text:
Plan started with 2.00 SOL ($202). This plan holds SOL, BTC, ETH and JUP only while each trades above its 20-day average. Today none does: SOL is 4.0% below, BTC 1.7% below, ETH 4.2% below and JUP 11.0% below.

So the plan moves to USDC and waits. Holding SOL as 'cash' would still lose money if SOL keeps falling (it is down 14.5% in 30 days). As soon as an asset closes back above its average, the plan buys it.

Devil's advocate: trend rules buy late and sell late; if the market bounces tomorrow, we will miss the first few percent. We accept that, because this plan exists to avoid the big drops, not to catch every move.

title: First positions: GTA6 and SI
text:

GTA6 ($7.2M market cap, 25.8K holders, $401K liquidity): a meme built around the GTA VI release on November 19, after this plan's first review window, so the story should keep building. Our anti-rug check found no group of top holders funded by the same wallet. The same brain bought it for the live desk yesterday.

SI ($14.3M, 52K holders, top 10 hold 11%): real, irregular trading volume worth 34% of its value per day, up 45% in three days and 20% below its weekly high. Anti-rug: clean (largest common-funder group holds 1.7%).

Devil's advocate: GTA6 is up 56% in 24 hours, so we are buying after a run, not on a pullback; a 30% stop can fill lower if it drops fast. SI's creator has launched about 7,500 tokens, the profile of a token factory, even though the holders look spread out. We accept it with a 30% stop on each and modest size, so a worst case costs about a fifth of the plan.

title: Selling DOAS: the automatic buy broke a rule
text:
The automatic brain bought DOAS at 16:07 ART with idle cash. That was a filter mistake, not a bet: DOAS has been on our fabricated-volume list since October 27 (bots trading the same amount every hour), and the scan data was inconsistent (−98% in 24 hours, 2% of its 3-day high). The filter blocked overheated tokens but not collapsed ones.

Selling now, close to the entry price; the cost is the round-trip fee and slippage (about 3%, roughly $2). The brain is fixed: it now only buys a healthy pullback (55–90% of the 3-day high, between −40% and +60% in 24 hours), with daily volume of at least 30% of market cap, 1,000+ holders, a scan less than 2.5 hours old, and a fabricated-volume blacklist.

title: Selling USELESS: one wallet funded holders with 15% of the supply
text: Tonight's anti-rug check looks at who funded the 20 largest holders of each coin. USELESS came back CONCENTRATED: four of its biggest holders, together 15.3% of all tokens, were set up and paid for by the same wallet (D89hHJT5…), and I could not confirm that wallet belongs to an exchange. A single hidden owner of 15% can sell into everyone else at any moment, so under this plan's rules the coin goes. The position was bought a few hours ago by the automatic trend rule, which does not run this check before buying; it is down about 2%, so the exit costs little. The money stays in the plan's cash for the next coin that passes the check. STONK also showed a 4-wallet group (4.2%), but those wallets were funded by a Binance hot wallet, which is normal for coins traded on exchanges, so it stays. SPX is clean.
